chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fazalah ibn Ayoub, from Umar ibn Aban, from Isa ibn Abu Mansur, who said:
I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), along with Ibn Abu Yafour and Abdullah ibn Talha. So he began by saying to him: 'O Ibn Abu Yafour!'

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Six characteristics, whoever possesses them will be in front of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and on the right of Allah.' Ibn Abu Yafour said: 'And what are they? May I be sacrificed for you.'

A Muslim man should love for his brother what he loves for the dearest of his family, and a Muslim man should dislike for his brother what he dislikes for the dearest of his family, and advise him regarding Wilayah.
So Ibn Abu Yafour wept and said: 'And how should he advise him regarding Wilayah?'

He said: 'O Ibn Abu Yafour! When he is at that station, his concern is his primary focus. So he rejoices in his joy if he rejoices, and grieves in his grief if he grieves. And if he has something that can relieve him, he relieves him; otherwise, he supplicates to Allah for him.'
He said: Then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three are for you and three are for us: that you recognize our merit, and tread upon our heels (follow us closely), and await our outcome.'
So whoever is like this will be in front of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and those who are below them will be illuminated by their light.
And as for those on the right of Allah, if those below them were to see them, life would not be pleasant for them due to what they see of their merit.
So Ibn Abu Yafour said: 'And what is the matter with them that they do not see them, while they are on the right of Allah?'

He said: 'O Ibn Abu Yafour! They are veiled by the Light of Allah. Has not the hadith reached you that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say: 'Indeed, for Allah there are creatures on the right of the Throne, in front of Allah and on the right of Allah.'
Their faces are whiter than snow and brighter than the shining sun. The questioner asks, 'Who are these?' So it is said, 'These are those who loved each other for the Majesty of Allah.'

key_terms.بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ: In front of Allah (a position of honor)
key_terms.عَنْ يَمِينِ اللَّهِ: On the right of Allah (a position of high status)

ai.seo_question: What are the six characteristics that place a believer in front of Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the spiritual station of those who embody mutual love and sincere advice regarding Wilayah, a concept central to Shia theology linking emotional solidarity with political and spiritual allegiance. It further distinguishes the Imams' unique status as being veiled by Allah's light, referencing the tradition of the 'people of love' (Ashab al-Tahabbud) near the Throne, thereby elevating the believer's connection to the Ahl al-Bayt as a means of divine proximity.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Umar Bin Aban, from Isa Bin Abu Mansour who said,
‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, I and Ibn Abu Yafour, and Abdullah Bin Talha. So he<sup>asws</sup> said, initiating him: ‘O Ibn Abu Yafour!

Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Six characteristics, the one who has these in him, would be in front of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic and upon the right of (the Throne of) Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’’. So Ibn Abu Yafour said, ‘And what are these, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>?’

Heasws said: ‘A Muslim person should love for his brother what he loves for the dearest of his family, and a Muslim person should dislike for his brother what he dislikes for the dearest of his family, and advise him for the Wilayah’.
So Ibn Abu Yafour wept and said, ‘And how should he advise him for the Wilayah?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said ‘O Ibn Abu Yafour! When there was that status from him, his endeavours would be his main concern. So he would be happy for his happiness if he was happy, and grieve for his grief if he was in grief; and if it was so that there was in his presence what could relieve him, so he should relieve him, or else supplicate to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for him’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Three are for you and three are for us<sup>asws</sup> - that you should recognise our<sup>asws</sup> merits, and obediently follow us<sup>asws</sup>, and await our<sup>asws</sup> end result (Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup>).
So the ones who were (observe) like this, would be in front of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and they would illuminate by their light the ones who were below them.

And as for those on the right of (the Throne of) Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so if the ones who were below them were to see them, the life would not be welcoming for them due to what they would be seeing from their merits.
So Ibn Abu Yafour said, ‘And what is the matter with them that they would not be seeing them, and the would be on the right (of the Throne) of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>?’

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Ibn Abu Yafour! They would be veiled by the Light of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. Has not the Hadeeth reached you that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘For Allah<sup>azwj</sup> there are creatures on the right of the Throne, in front of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and on the right of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>.

Their faces would be whiter than the snow, and more illuminating than the shining sun. The asking one would ask, ‘What are they?’ So it would be said: ‘They are those who used to love regarding the Majesty of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from ‘Amr ibn Aban from ‘Isa ibn abu Mansur who has said the following: “Once ibn abu Ya’fur, ‘Abd Allah ibn Talha and I were in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who on his own initiation said, ‘O ibn abu Ya’fur, the Messenger of Allah has said, “There are six things that if found in a person, he will be before Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, to the right of Allah (to the right of the Throne of Allah).”’ Ibn abu Ya’fur then asked, ‘What are those things, may Allah keep my soul in service for your cause?’

The Imam said, ‘A man must love for his Muslim brother what he loves for the most beloved person of his family and dislike for his Muslim brother what he dislikes for the most beloved person of his family and enlighten him in Walayah (the position of people who possess Divine Authority).’

Ibn abu Ya’fur then wept and asked, ‘How does he enlighten about Walayah r T The Imam said, ‘O ibn abu Ya’fur, if he is of the same level (of belief), he should encourage him, show happiness in his happiness and express sadness if he is sad. If he has the means to facilitate him he should do so if not he should pray to Allah for him.

’ “The narrator has said that abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) then said, ‘Three things are for you and three things are for us. What is for us is that you must learn about our excellent merits, follow our footsteps and wait for our end results (Divine Kingdom) to take place.
Whoever has these facts will be before Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, and those below them will receive light from their light.
On seeing those who will be to the right of Allah, the ones below will not feel happy because of the enviable merits of the persons above.’
Ibn abu Ya’fur then asked, ‘How is it that they will not see when they are on the right of Allah?’
The Imam said, ‘O ibn abu Ya’fur, they are veiled with the light of Allah.

Are you not aware of the Hadith that the Messenger of Allah said, ‘Allah has a creature on the right of the Throne before Allah and on the right of Allah their faces are whiter than snow and brighter than the sun of the midday. Someone asks, ‘Who are they?’ It will be said, ‘These are the ones who loved each other in the Glory of Allah.’”
